items.line: Smolensk cut regional payments to families of the killed from 1 million to 700,000 roubles.
items.quote: regional payments to the families of those killed in the war in Ukraine have been cut from 1 million rubles [$12,300] to 700,000 rubles [$8,630]
items.more: A CIT weekly note, 18 to 25 Oct.

items.line: Payments to soldiers and to families of the dead passed 3 trillion roubles in six months; sign-up bonuses alone cost over 600 billion, over 500 billion of it regional.
items.quote: has exceeded 3 trillion rubles [$36 billion] over a six-month period
items.quote2: sign-up bonuses alone cost the Kremlin more than 600 billion rubles [$7 billion] per six months, of which more than 500 billion is covered by regional budgets
items.more: An estimate by the Re: Russia project as relayed in CIT's weekly mobilisation note; the underlying Re: Russia dataset was not opened.

items.line: Novosibirsk cut its regional sign-up bonus from 2.5 to 1.6 million roubles.
items.quote: from 2.5 million rubles [$29,900], set in April this year, to 1.6 million rubles
items.more: A CIT weekly note, 11 to 18 Oct. This page's bonus chart is not changed by it: its rates come from the regional summary read on 28 Oct.

items.line: Contracts signed: 29,900 in September (31,900 a year earlier) and 263,000 in January to September (292,000). Cost per contract 1.9 million roubles, up from 1.4 million.
items.quote: recruitment reached 29,900 (last year: 31,900) in September, bringing the total to 263,000 new contract soldiers over the first three quarters (last year: 292,000)
items.quote2: is still 1.9 million rubles, almost 30% higher than a year ago (1.4 million rubles)
items.more: Estimated from Russian regional budget spending, so a floor for contracts with a regional bonus; Kluge puts the pace at about 1,000 a day. Of the cost per contract, he divides all regional recruitment spending in his dataset by the number of contracts.

items.line: Nizhny Tagil paid recruitment agents 400,000 roubles a head: 580 men delivered in 2025 for 260 million roubles, per the city prosecutor.
items.quote: a recruitment agent receives 400,000 rubles ($4,500) for each new contract soldier he manages to recruit
items.quote2: In 2025, agents in Nizhny Tagil delivered 580 men to recruitment offices, and 260 million rubles were paid out in return
items.more: The prosecutor asked the city duma to stop the payouts, citing criminal gangs; the deputy mayor refused, saying they help meet quotas.

items.outlet: War on the Rocks (Whisler and Kofman)
items.line: About 1.3 million contract soldiers recruited since 2022, against 300,000 mobilised in 2022; the 2026 target of 409,000 is not on track.
items.quote: the 300,000 reservists called up pale in comparison to the roughly 1.3 million contract soldiers Moscow has since recruited
items.quote2: goal is to recruit 409,000 contract personnel in 2026, but it is not on track to meet that target
items.more: The authors also give about 35,000 recruits a month in 2025 against a similar number killed and seriously wounded, a 2025 target of 403,000 that was slightly exceeded, and about 700,000 personnel in and around Ukraine.

items.line: Named list: 7,920 officers confirmed dead by 23 Oct; volunteers have been the largest group of named dead since September 2024.
items.quote: By October 23, 2026, the death of 7,920 officers of the Russian army and other security agencies had been confirmed
items.quote2: By September 2024, volunteers once again emerged as the largest category among the
items.more: The officer share of deaths fell from up to 10% early in the war to 2 to 3% by November 2024.

items.line: More than 450 Peruvians joined the Russian army, per Peru's foreign ministry; 21 trafficking investigations cover more than 300 victims.
items.quote: По данным МИД Перу, всего в ВС РФ вступили более 450 граждан страны
items.quote2: Сейчас перуанские прокуроры ведут 21 расследование по делам о торговле людьми, еще одно расследование связано с обвинениями в организованной преступности. Пострадавшими по этим делам проходят более 300 человек
items.more: One lawyer for the families puts the number above 1,000. iStories worked with the Peruvian podcast La Encerrona; recruiters were routed through Ufa and Meleuz in Bashkortostan.

items.line: Irkutsk region will pay 1.5 million roubles for each foreigner recruited; Smolensk offers 1.1 million until 1 December.
items.quote: Власти Иркутской области готовы платить по 1,5 млн рублей за привлеченного иностранца
items.quote2: до 1 декабря 2026 года вербовщики могут получить 1,1 млн рублей
items.more: Payments to recruiters, not to the recruit.

items.outlet: Meduza, citing Bloomberg and the MSMT report
items.line: Up to 25,000 North Korean workers may be making military drones in Russia; 15,000 to 30,000 North Korean workers were in Russia in late 2025. Workers, not troops.
items.quote: As many as 25,000 North Korean citizens may be working in military drone production in Russia
items.quote2: between 15,000 and 30,000 North Korean citizens were working in Russia
items.more: From the report of the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, which includes the United States, South Korea, Japan and eight other countries.

items.line: Claim by Ukrainian military intelligence: a North Korean missile unit of about 90 people could get up to 120 missiles in Voronezh region. Not independently confirmed.
items.quote: The unit numbers about 90 people and will be folded into
items.quote2: it could receive up to 120 North Korean ballistic missiles
items.more: Reported by Reuters from a statement by Andrii Cherniak of Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate.

items.line: North Korea sent at least 29,488 containers, an estimated 8 to 11 million shells and rockets, from Sep 2023 to Jan 2026; shipments have since fallen sharply.
items.quote: получила как минимум 29488 контейнеров с вооружениями из КНДР. По оценке OSC, это соответствует от 8 до 11 млн артиллерийских снарядов и ракет
items.quote2: С начала 2026-го «Важные истории» и OSC обнаружили только одну поставку из КНДР
items.more: Munitions, not people: an estimate from ship records and satellite images. The tracker account re-posted the article on 28 Jul 2026.

items.line: Garrison military courts sentenced 8,781 people in the first half of 2026, 42% more than a year earlier (6,192).
items.quote: military courts handed down sentences to 8,781 people in the first half of this year
items.quote2: 42% more than in the first half of last year , when 6,192 people were convicted
items.more: Serving soldiers and others tried by military courts; it is not a count of prisoners recruited for the army. No new prisoner-recruit totals appeared in the eight accounts this week.

items.line: Omsk: online reviews of the Sirius-55 recruitment centre say residents are picked up off the street and made to sign.
items.quote: say city residents are being forced to sign contracts with Russia's Defense Ministry and go to war
items.more: Reviews on the 2GIS map page, flagged by the Omsk Civic Association; the reviews are unverified.

items.line: Rights groups report men forced to sign contracts in at least 33 regions and Crimea, in complaints from 12 Aug to 12 Oct. Conscripts excluded.
items.quote: как минимум в 33 регионах России и в аннексированном Крыму
items.quote2: Жалобы поступали в период с 12 августа по 12 октября
items.more: Verstka's headline says 34 regions and its text says 33 plus Crimea; the text figure is used. Complaints went to four rights groups, and most came from Udmurtia, Omsk and Penza regions.
